target_object_registry.definition: Each arm has a fixed unknown distribution nu_i supported on [0,1], with mean mu_i. Selecting arm i produces a fresh independent sample. Cumulative pseudo-regret is computed from the means.

comparators.definition: Largest mean $\mu_\star$ of the fixed distributions; the best arm need not be unique.

norms.definition: The model specifies coordinate ranges of finite vectors. Discrete action labels have no derivative order. A placeholder norm imposes no additional geometric assumption.

objects.definition: Each arm has a fixed unknown distribution nu_i supported on [0,1], with mean mu_i. Selecting arm i produces a fresh independent sample. Cumulative pseudo-regret is computed from the means.
The mean μ_i belongs to the ith fixed reward distribution. It is unknown and cannot be queried directly.

protocols.adversary_information: The unknown distribution or parameter is fixed before interaction. Learner randomness and sample randomness are independent. No adversary changes the distribution round by round from the learner's history.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: The selected arm determines the mean gap mu_*-mu_{a_t}; the objective does not use the best realized reward path in hindsight.
protocols.past_requery: No new information may be requested from past rounds or previously used samples. Received feedback may be stored and processed. In a stochastic model, an action may be repeated in a new round, with a fresh charged sample.
protocols.queries_per_round: One arm pull and one scalar sample per round, under fixed budget T.
steps: The action $a_t$ is chosen from the history and private randomness.
A fresh sample $Y_t$ from that arm is observed.
Pseudo-regret uses $\mu_\star-\mu_{a_t}$, while feedback remains only $Y_t$.
